samples.summary: Rationale for excluding GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL now exists in four places and will diverge
samples.evidence: oauth-state.ts:214-232 spells out the whole decision (why Google's URL is not read, what the alternative would have broken, and the one deployment shape that pays for it). The same argument is restated in github-auth.guard.ts:78-83, in the spec comment oauth-state.spec.ts:156-166, in packages/backend/README.md:63-83, in packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:455-462, and in docs/tasks/active/20260915-google-oauth-login-lessons.md:34-45. The repo's convention is that decision history lives in the task/lessons doc and the canonical subsystem doc (docs/design/backend.md), with code comments pointing at them; carrying five prose copies of a reverted alternative means a later change to the resolution order updates some and leaves the others stating the opposite. Cost stays inside the codebase, hence minor.

samples.summary: Canonical subsystem doc does not record that GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL is deliberately excluded from useSecureCookies()
samples.evidence: docs/design/backend.md is the canonical doc for this subsystem and its cookie section (lines 563-579) plus the CLI-gate bullets (188-203) still describe the resolution order as "COOKIE_SECURE first, then GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL's scheme, then NODE_ENV" with no mention of a second provider. The delta's whole point is that a *now-existing* second callback URL variable is intentionally not part of that order, and the consequence (an https Google-only install with NODE_ENV!=production mints unprefixed, non-Secure session/state cookies unless it sets COOKIE_SECURE=true) is a deployment-visible design decision recorded only in self-hosting.md:455 and the task lessons file. CONTRIBUTING expects such a decision folded into the canonical design doc rather than only into user docs. Note docs/design/backend.md is a TOP-LEVEL design doc, so its backticked paths are lane-checked, but omitted prose is not.

samples.summary: callbackScheme() is now a parameterised helper with a single call site
